craft_claim: Metre and rhythmic structure aid encoding, recall, and performance, which is why cadenced language feels like it is carrying meaning rather than decorating it.

supporting_evidence.location: Memory in Oral Traditions (Oxford University Press), chapters on metre, rhyme, and formula
supporting_evidence.note: Rubin assembles experimental and corpus evidence that metre, rhyme, and formulaic structure function as encoding and retrieval devices that make long verbal works performable and memorable.

scope: Verse, refrain, chant, memorable prose, and any long text designed to be remembered or performed.
exceptions: Modern bureaucratic or reference prose, where memorability is not a goal and regularity may impede scanning.
